text:
anya: Quick check — after the Terraform apply earlier some model runtime toggles disappeared from the cluster. Services reading the ConfigMap `model-runtime` are getting empty values for a handful of models.

mike: Which apply exactly? @linh pushed something a few minutes ago?

linh: yep that was me. I adjusted the module that syncs our per-model configs from S3 -> k8s. I added a for-expression to flatten maps and set a default, but might've coerced nulls into empty strings. Branch: `fix/configmap-null`.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by linh — `terraform apply` (run id: tf-1835004319). Plan applied.

anya: Can you paste the ConfigMap that ended up in the cluster? I saw `model-x` with an empty string which breaks the runtime parsing.

linh: here's what I saw in the cluster: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-runtime
  namespace: infra
data:
  model-x: ""
  model-y: "enable_fast_path=false"
```

linh: The for-expression I used was basically `data = { for k, v in local.models : k => v }` and I added a `v ?? ""` to be safe. That turned null -> "".

mike: Empty string vs missing key matters — our runtime treats empty string as explicit override to disable all flags. Not great. Can we hotfix the CM until TF patch lands?

anya: Yes. Quick patch we can run now (kubectl):
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap model-runtime --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/model-x","value":"enable_special_cache=true"}]'
```

linh: Applied the patch and restarted the runtime pod. Logs show model-x flags are back and no immediate errors.

mike: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) open a PR to fix the null handling in TF, 2) add a simple TF test or Terratest check to ensure we do not write empty-string values for keys that should be absent. Also add a changelog entry so we know why this happened.

linh: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/487 — includes `v != null ? v : null` logic and a unit test for the tpl that generates the config. I also added a CI job to run `kubectl diff` against a test cluster.

anya: For deploy safety can we stop TF from overwriting CM when nothing meaningfully changed? Maybe compute a sha annotation and only update object if sha differs. That would avoid churn from generated-empty-values.

mike: Agreed. Another option: have Terraform manage a `ConfigMap` resource but use `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [data] }` and manage the data via a small controller or a null_resource that triggers only on sha changes. We should choose the least-blinky approach.

linh: I'll add a `local.sha = sha256(join(";", [for k in sort(keys(local.models)) : k+":"+(local.models[k] != null ? local.models[k] : "")] ))` and then a `null_resource` with `triggers = { sha = local.sha }` to only push when sha changes. Patch in the PR.

anya: Great. Can @mike review and merge the PR once CI passes? Then we can roll forward the TF and avoid another emergency hotfix.

mike: On it — reviewing now. Also let's add a short runbook step in infra runbook: "When model-runtime has empty values, run kubectl patch to restore the expected key/value and then revert TF change."

linh: Added runbook entry in the PR description.

anya: Thanks everyone. Logged board card infra-342 for follow-up and risk review. Will update stake-holders. :thumbsup:

mike: thx.
